cluster_stories.title: US takes step to halt Nvidia AI chip shipments to Chinese firms outside China
cluster_stories.summary: The US Department of Commerce on Sunday moved to close a year-old potential loophole it had created that may have led companies to export ‌the world’s most advanced chips – such as Nvidia’s most sophisticated Rubin and Blackwell processors, as well as AMD’s MI350x – to Chinese entities located outside China. The unexpected guidance suggests the United States’ best artificial intelligence chips may have been making their way to the subsidiaries of Chinese AI firms based in places such as Malaysia...

cluster_stories.title: Arm Holdings CEO says US would have difficulty banning AI CPU chip exports to China
cluster_stories.summary: Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas said on ‌Tuesday ⁠that ⁠it would ​be difficult to block the export ​of CPUs to China that ​are ⁠useful for ‌AI ​because of ​their widespread ⁠use and as it would ​be difficult to ​only block AI CPUs.

cluster_stories.title: Nvidia’s AI Chips Sought by Chinese Labs With Ties to Military
cluster_stories.summary: At least seven Chinese universities that support the country’s armed forces and defense industry are seeking access to Nvidia Corp.’s H200 chips, the most powerful artificial intelligence processors ever allowed by the US to be sold in China, according to a review of procurement records.

polls.description: Chinese AI company DeepSeek's historic $7 billion funding round at $59 billion valuation marks a major milestone in China's AI development and global competition.
polls.question: Is DeepSeek's rise a threat to US AI dominance or healthy competition?

cluster_stories.title: DeepSeek lines up its first outside money: a $7bn round at up to $59bn
cluster_stories.summary: DeepSeek has spent eighteen months as the most talked-about AI lab that almost nobody could invest in. That is about to change. cluster_stories.headline: DEEPSEEK RAISES $7B AT $59B VALUATION... FIRST OUTSIDE FUNDING

cluster_stories.title: DeepSeek Close to Sealing $7 Billion Funding in Historic AI Deal
cluster_stories.summary: DeepSeek is close to finalizing a deal to raise about 50 billion yuan ($7.4 billion) from investors including Tencent Holdings Ltd. and its own founder in one of China’s largest startup financings, a milestone for a domestic AI industry seeking capital to take on marquee US names like OpenAI.
